methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A region-wide AI readiness initiative signals intentional capability-building outside NoVA, but success depends on whether this translates into distributed deep expertise or remains a planning exercise—critical test case for Build It Yourself potential in mid-tier metros.

signals.title: Warner, Anthropic launch AI pilot to help Hampton Roads military families find local resources - The Legacy Newspaper
signals.signal_reading: Senator Warner deploying Anthropic's platform AI to solve military family navigation problems exemplifies shallow-but-useful distribution—Hampton Roads gets access to advanced capability without building indigenous expertise, reinforcing platform dependency over local development.

signals.title: AI is already common in Virginia Beach high schools. Leaders weigh guardrails - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: AI already pervasive in Virginia Beach schools with leaders now seeking guardrails indicates rapid platform-driven adoption outpacing governance—classic shallow distribution where tools spread faster than understanding, raising questions about sustainable capability development.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Axios reporting AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce without corresponding training infrastructure signals anxiety without capability—neither deep expertise nor broad fluency materializing, just displacement concerns that could widen metro-rural and skills gaps.

signals.title: Norfolk Public Library to teach people about AI - Yahoo
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Public Library teaching AI literacy represents grassroots peer-to-peer capability building through civic infrastructure—if scaled through Virginia's library networks, this model could distribute foundational fluency beyond elite tech hubs and educational institutions.
